research_question: In adults with early-stage (T1-T2) clinically node-negative oral cavity squamous cell carcinoma, including oral tongue, does elective (immediate, prophylactic) neck dissection at the time of primary tumour resection improve disease-free survival (time to new disease, disease progression or death) compared with therapeutic (delayed) neck dissection after watchful waiting with dissection only on nodal relapse?
treatment_label: Elective (immediate, prophylactic) neck dissection at time of primary tumour surgery
control_label: Therapeutic (delayed) neck dissection — observation/watchful waiting with dissection only on nodal relapse
outcome_description: Disease-free survival (also reported as event-free, relapse-free or recurrence-free survival): time from randomisation to recurrence, disease progression, new disease or death from any cause, expressed as a hazard ratio with 95% confidence interval for elective versus therapeutic neck dissection. Prefer the intention-to-treat analysis at the longest reported follow-up; convert the 95% CI to a standard error of the log HR. If no DFS hazard ratio is reported but a log-rank test with observed/expected events, or per-arm event counts with a log-rank p-value, are available, estimate the log HR and its variance using Peto's (O-E)/V or Parmar's indirect methods and state the method used. Invert the HR (and swap the interval) if reported as therapeutic versus elective. Overall-survival-only hazard ratios are not used for this outcome.
positive_direction: A positive effect (HR below 1 on the hazard-ratio scale) means longer disease-free survival — fewer recurrence/progression/death events — with elective neck dissection than with therapeutic (delayed) neck dissection, i.e. the result favours elective neck dissection.
search_queries: elective neck dissection versus observation node-negative oral cavity cancer randomized trial
prophylactic neck dissection early oral squamous cell carcinoma disease-free survival trial
watchful waiting therapeutic neck dissection oral tongue cancer N0 controlled trial outcome
inclusion_criteria: Randomised controlled trial in adults with early-stage oral cavity (including oral tongue) squamous cell carcinoma and a clinically node-negative (cN0) neck
Compares elective/immediate neck dissection at the time of primary tumour surgery with observation/watchful waiting followed by therapeutic neck dissection on nodal relapse

Reports some quantitative survival or recurrence outcome data from which a disease-free/event-free survival hazard ratio can be obtained or indirectly estimated (HR with CI, log-rank statistics, or per-arm events with log-rank p-value)
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study (systematic review, meta-analysis, narrative review, editorial, opinion piece, commentary, protocol or purely theoretical/modelling paper)

No comparison between a treatment and a control condition — single-arm or case-series studies, non-randomised/observational comparisons, and trials evaluating only radiotherapy or sentinel lymph node biopsy
No quantitative outcome data that can produce an effect size (no hazard ratio with CI, no log-rank/observed-expected statistics, no per-arm event counts with p-value, no means+SDs or proportions)
Completely unrelated to the research topic (not early-stage clinically node-negative oral cavity squamous cell carcinoma, or not about timing of neck dissection)
moderators_to_extract: Tumour site (oral tongue only vs mixed oral cavity subsites)
Tumour stage distribution (T1 vs T2 vs mixed)
Extent of elective dissection (supraomohyoid/selective vs modified radical/comprehensive)
Risk of bias / allocation concealment and blinding of outcome assessment
Method used to obtain HR (directly reported vs Peto/Parmar indirect estimation)
effect_size_note: Pool log hazard ratios with inverse-variance random-effects (REML/DerSimonian-Laird) meta-analysis; HR oriented as elective versus therapeutic so HR < 1 favours elective neck dissection. SE(log HR) derived from the reported 95% CI, or from Peto's (O-E)/V or Parmar's indirect methods when only log-rank statistics or per-arm events with a log-rank p-value are available; studies with neither are excluded from this outcome. Report heterogeneity (tau², I², Q) and assess small-study effects if ≥10 trials.
